questions.question: The average of the ages of A, B and C , 3 years ago was 45 years, and that of B and C 4 years ago was 35 years. Find the age of A after 4 years.
questions.questionHtml: The average of the ages of A, B and C , 3 years ago was 45 years, and that of B and C 4 years ago was 35 years. Find the age of A after 4 years.
questions.solution:
Given,

Average age of A, B and C, 3 years ago = 45

Average age of A, B and C at present = 45 + 3 =48

Sum of ages of A, B and C (A + B + C) = 48 × 3 = 144

Given,

Average age of B and C, 4 years ago = 35

Average age of B and C at present = 35 + 4 = 39

Sum of ages of B and C (B + C) = 39 × 2 = 78

Age of A at present= (A + B + C) - (B + C)

= 144 - 78

= 66

Age of A after 4 years = 66 + 4 = 70 years.

So, the age of A, after 4 years is 70 years.

Hence, the correct answer is 70.

Statement: Nashit wore his uniform, loaded his gun and left for work in his chauffeur - driven official car. Assumptions: I. Nashit is an officer in the armed forces. II. Nashit is a military commando posted at Raj Bhavan, Jaipur.
questions.questionHtml:
This question has a statement followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. Assuming that all information given in the statement is true, consider the given conclusions and determine which of them logically and definitely follows from the given statement.

Statement:

Nashit wore his uniform, loaded his gun and left for work in his chauffeur - driven official car.

Assumptions:

I. Nashit is an officer in the armed forces.

II. Nashit is a military commando posted at Raj Bhavan, Jaipur.

options.text: Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
options.html: Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

questions.solution:
Statement: Nashit wore his uniform, loaded his gun and left for work in his chauffeur-driven official car.

Assumption I: Nashit is an officer in the armed forces. While the details (uniform, gun, official car) suggest a high-ranking security or military role, they are not exclusive to the "armed forces." He could be a high-ranking police officer, a paramilitary officer, or part of a specialised security detail. Because the statement doesn't specify the branch of service, this is a possibility, but not a definitively true assumption. This is not implicit.

Assumption II: Nashit is a military commando posted at Raj Bhavan, Jaipur. This assumption is far too specific. The statement mentions nothing about his specific unit (commando) or his specific location (Raj Bhavan, Jaipur). This is not implicit.

Hence, the correct answer is "Neither assumption I nor II is implicit".

questions.question: What is the friction force employed between the two surfaces interacted in relative speed?
questions.questionHtml: What is the friction force employed between the two surfaces interacted in relative speed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dynamic Friction

Key Points

  • Friction is the force that opposes the relative motion of two surfaces in contact.
  • Rolling friction is always less than static friction, limiting friction, and dynamic friction.
  • When one object rolls over the surface of another object, the resistance to its motion is called rolling friction.
    • Rolling reduces the effect of friction.
    • It is always easier to roll than to slide a body over another due to the effect of rolling friction.
    • Rolling friction is less than sliding friction.
    • Ball-bearing work on the principle of rolling friction.
    • Ball bearings are used in cycles, scooters to reduce friction between wheel and axle.
  • The substance which reduces the friction between the moving surface is called lubricants.
  • Kinetic friction is the frictional force that occurs when two objects are moving relative to each other or rub together.
    • Kinetic friction is also called dynamic friction.
  • The force which acts in a direction opposite to the direction of motion is called static friction.
    • Static friction is greater than kinetic friction.
  • Sliding friction is the resistance created by two objects when one object is sliding over another.
    • Sliding friction is smaller than static friction.
  • Limiting friction is the maximum value of static friction when two surfaces come in contact with each other.

questions.question: Who hoisted the flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay on 9 th August 1942 during the Quit India Movement?
questions.questionHtml: Who hoisted the flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay on 9<sup>th</sup> August 1942 during the Quit India Movement?
questions.solution: Aruna Asaf Ali, known as the "Grand Old Lady" of India's independence movement, hoisted the Indian flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay on 9th August 1942 during the Quit India Movement. The movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi to end British rule and was marked by the slogan "Do or Die". The immediate cause for the movement was the failure of the Cripps Mission, which offered Dominion Status to India, along with partition. The movement was also fueled by Indian involvement in World War II without prior consultation, prevalence of anti-British sentiment, centralization of many small movements, and shortage of essential commodities.

questions.question: How many basic talams are there in Indian Classical Carnatic music?

questions.solution: In Indian Classical Carnatic music, there are 7 basic talams: Dhruva, Matya, Rupaka, Jhampa, Triputa, Ata, and Eka. Each talam has a unique structure that maintains rhythm in compositions. These basic talams can be expanded into 35 talams by applying five jatis (types of rhythmic units). Talam is crucial in Carnatic music, providing the rhythmic framework for performances.

Key Points

  • Bara-lacha Pass is a high-altitude mountain pass located in the Himalayan Range, not in the Western Ghats.
  • The pass is situated on the Manali-Leh highway at an elevation of 4,890 meters (16,043 feet).
  • Bara-lacha Pass acts as a crucial connector between Lahaul district in Himachal Pradesh and Leh district in Ladakh.
  • The pass is also known as the "Pass with crossroads" since it is located at the meeting point of roads connecting Spiti, Ladakh, Zanskar, and Lahaul regions.
  • Being part of the Trans-Himalayan region, Bara-lacha Pass is a strategic and scenic location for travelers and trekkers alike.

Additional Information

  • Western Ghats
    • The Western Ghats is a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India.
    • It is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its biodiversity.
    • It spans states like Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.
  • Himalayas
    • The Himalayas are the world's highest mountain range, spanning five countries: India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, and Pakistan.
    • They are home to many of the planet's highest peaks, including Mount Everest and K2.
    • The range is crucial for India's climate, as it influences monsoon patterns and acts as a climate barrier.
  • Key Passes in India

questions.question: Among the following four Vedas, which one is considered to be the origin of Indian music?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sama Veda.

Key Points

  • Sama Veda is considered the origin of Indian music and is often referred to as the "Veda of melodies and chants."
  • It primarily contains hymns and chants that are meant to be sung rather than recited, providing the foundation for musical scales and compositions in Indian classical music.
  • The chants in Sama Veda were designed to invoke divine blessings and establish a spiritual connection, making it highly significant in religious rituals. Hence, the correct option is Sama Veda.
  • The hymns in Sama Veda are derived from the Rig Veda, but they are set to specific melodies or tunes, which are believed to be the precursor to the musical traditions of India.
  • Sama Veda is closely associated with Indian classical music, including the development of raga systems, which form the core of both Hindustani and Carnatic music traditions.

Additional Information

  • Sama Veda:
    • Sama Veda is one of the four Vedas and holds an integral place in the spiritual and musical traditions of ancient India.
    • It consists of 1,875 verses, most of which are derived from the Rig Veda. These verses are set to music and are intended for liturgical purposes.
    • Sama Veda lays the foundation for Indian musical traditions and emphasizes the importance of melodic chanting to enhance spiritual experience.
  • Comparison of the Four Vedas:
    • Rig Veda: Focuses on hymns and praises dedicated to the gods. It is the oldest and most foundational text in the Vedic literature.
    • Sama Veda: Contains musical chants and melodies derived from the Rig Veda, forming the basis of Indian music.
    • Yajur Veda: Deals with the rituals and ceremonies associated with sacrifices and practical aspects of religious worship.
    • Atharva Veda: Focuses on practical knowledge, spells, charms, and everyday life aspects, including medicine and healing practices.
  • Indian Music and Sama Veda:
    • Indian classical music evolved from the melodic structures outlined in Sama Veda, particularly the raga system.
    • Both Hindustani and Carnatic music traditions trace their roots to the Sama Veda, highlighting its significance in shaping the musical heritage of India.

Important Points

  • Historical Significance:
    • Sama Veda played a crucial role in the development of religious rituals and ceremonies in ancient India.
    • The musical chants of Sama Veda were used in temple rituals and were believed to have divine powers to connect humans with the spiritual realm.
  • Role in Music Evolution:
    • Sama Veda is considered the earliest source of Indian classical music, influencing not only music but also dance and drama traditions.
    • The raga system, which forms the backbone of Indian classical music, finds its origins in the melodic structures outlined in Sama Veda.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the terms of credit?

The correct answer is Source of credit.

Key Points

  • The terms of credit refer to the conditions under which loans are granted, ensuring clarity and security for both lenders and borrowers.
  • Source of credit does not constitute a component of the terms of credit. It refers to the entity or institution providing the loan, such as banks, cooperative societies, or moneylenders, but is not directly tied to the contractual terms of the loan.
  • The terms of credit typically include collateral, interest rate, and documentation, which are essential in determining the repayment capacity and risk involved in lending.
  • Collateral is an asset pledged by the borrower to the lender as security for the loan, ensuring repayment in case of default.
  • Interest rate refers to the cost of borrowing money, which is expressed as a percentage of the loan amount over a specified period.

Additional Information

  • Collateral:
    • Collateral is an important component of the terms of credit, as it secures the loan for the lender.
    • Common forms of collateral include property, gold, fixed deposits, or other valuable assets.
    • In case of default, the lender has the right to sell the collateral to recover the loan amount.
    • Collateral reduces the risk for lenders and encourages lending to borrowers with limited credit history.
  • Interest Rate:
    • The interest rate is the price charged by the lender for providing the loan.
    • It varies based on factors such as the type of loan, the borrower's creditworthiness, and market conditions.
    • Interest rates are typically expressed as annual percentages (e.g., Annual Percentage Rate or APR).
    • Lower interest rates make borrowing cheaper, while higher rates increase the cost of loans.
  • Documentation:
    • Documentation is another essential component of the terms of credit, ensuring legal enforceability of the loan agreement.
    • It includes proof of identity, income verification, credit history, and other relevant documents.
    • Proper documentation protects both lenders and borrowers by providing clarity on the loan terms, repayment schedule, and penalties.
    • Incomplete or incorrect documentation can lead to disputes or rejection of loan applications.

questions.question: Statement 1: The Earth's orbit around the Sun is nearly circular. Statement 2: Revolution of the Earth affects the length of a day
questions.questionHtml:
Statement 1: The Earth's orbit around the Sun is nearly circular.

Statement 2: Revolution of the Earth affects the length of a day
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Only Statement 1 is correct.

Key Points

Statement 1: The Earth's orbit around the Sun is nearly circular is correct because,-

  • Eccentricity of Earth's Orbit: The Earth's orbit around the Sun is elliptical with a low eccentricity of approximately 0.0167. This low value means the orbit is very close to being circular.
  • Consequences of Near-Circular Orbit: Because of this near-circular orbit, the variation in the Earth's distance from the Sun throughout the year (from perihelion to aphelion) is relatively small, affecting the amount of solar energy received but not drastically.
  • Astronomical Context: In astronomical terms, this low eccentricity contrasts sharply with the highly elliptical orbits of some other solar system bodies, which have much higher eccentricities.

Statement 2: Revolution of the Earth affects the length of a day is incorrect because,-

  • Earth’s Rotation Determines Day Length: The length of a day is governed by the Earth’s rotation on its axis. A single rotation on its axis takes approximately 24 hours, defining a solar day, and about 23 hours and 56 minutes for a sidereal day.
  • Misconception Clarification: The revolution of the Earth, which refers to its orbit around the Sun taking approximately 365.25 days, does not directly affect the length of a day. The minor variations in the length of a solar day throughout the year (known as the equation of time) are due to the Earth’s axial tilt and orbital eccentricity, but these are small deviations.
  • Day Length Stability: The Earth's axial rotation is fairly stable and isn’t significantly affected by its revolution around the Sun. This means that while the revolution does affect seasons and the calendar year, it doesn't influence the daily rotational period significantly.

Additional Information

  • Length of a Solar Day: The solar day, which is our standard 24-hour day, varies slightly throughout the year due to the elliptical shape of the orbit and axial tilt. This variation is minimal and follows a predictable annual pattern.Precession and Nutation: Over long periods, the Earth’s axial precession (a slow wobble with a period of about 26,000 years) can cause minor changes in the orientation of the Earth, but these changes are very gradual and have negligible impact on the day-to-day length.
  • Leap Years: To keep our calendar year synchronized with the Earth's orbit around the Sun, we have leap years. This adjustment involves adding an extra day every four years, compensating for the fact that the orbital period is about 365.25 days.

questions.question: A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 0.8 hour, while it comes back in 1.6 hour. If the speed of the stream be 5 km/hr, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.questionHtml: A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 0.8 hour, while it comes back in 1.6 hour. If the speed of the stream be 5 km/hr, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the boat in still water be x km/hr

Speed downstream = (x + 5) km/hr

Speed upstream = (x − 5) km/hr

Distance of downstream = Distance of Upstream

∴ (x + 5) × 0.8 = (x − 5) × 1.6 ⇒ 0.8x + 4 = 1.6x – 8

⇒ 0.8x = 12 km/hr ⇒ x = 15 km/hr

questions.question: On a sum of money, the compound interest for 2 years is Rs. 832, while the simple interest for the same time period is Rs.800, then find out the difference amount for period of 3 years?
questions.questionHtml: On a sum of money, the compound interest for 2 years is Rs. 832, while the simple interest for the same time period is Rs.800, then find out the difference amount for period of 3 years?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

SI for 1 year = 800 ÷ 2 = ₹400

Difference for 2 years = CI − SI = 832 − 800 = ₹32

Rate (R) = (Interest on 1st year SI ÷ 1st year SI) × 100 = (32 ÷ 400) × 100 = 8%

For 3 years, Difference = 3 × (2-year Diff) + (R% of 2-year Diff)

Difference = 3 × 32 + (8% of 32) = 96 + 2.56 = 98.56

∴ The correct answer is ₹98.56.

Alternate Method

Given:

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹832

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹800

Formula Used:

Difference for 2 years (D2) = P × (R ÷ 100)2

Difference for 3 years (D3) = 3 × D2 + (R% of D2)

Calculations:

⇒ SI for 1 year = Total SI ÷ 2 = 800 ÷ 2 = ₹400

⇒ Difference between CI and SI for 2 years (D2) = 832 − 800 = ₹32

⇒ The difference of ₹32 is the interest earned exactly on the first year's SI (₹400).

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (32 ÷ 400) × 100% = 8%

⇒ Difference for 3 years (D3) = 3 × D2 + (R% of D2)

⇒ D3 = 3 × 32 + (8 ÷ 100) × 32

⇒ D3 = 96 + 2.56

⇒ D3 = ₹98.56

∴ The correct answer is ₹98.56.

Additional Information

Tree Method for Compound Interest

It breaks down CI into simple interest and interest-on-interest components. The 1st row is always the Simple Interest. The lower rows sum up to represent the exact difference between CI and SI over the years.

CI vs SI Difference (2 Years)

Formula: Diff2 = P × (R ÷ 100)2. It strictly represents the interest generated on the first year's simple interest.

CI vs SI Difference (3 Years)

Formula: Diff3 = P × (R ÷ 100)2 × (3 + R ÷ 100). For fast calculation, simply multiply the 2-year difference by 3 and add the rate percentage of the 2-year difference.

questions.question: A square pyramid with side 10 cm has a volume of 400 cm 3 . Find the total surface area of the pyramid.
questions.questionHtml: A square pyramid with side 10 cm has a volume of 400 cm<sup>3</sup>. Find the total surface area of the pyramid.
questions.solution:
Formula used:

Volume of pyramid = 1/3 × Base area × Height

Calculation:

Base area of the pyramid = Area of square = (10)2 = 100 cm2

Volume of pyramid = 1/3 × Base area × Height

⇒ 400 = 1/3 × 100 × Height

⇒ Height of pyramid = 12 cm

Now,

⇒ Slant height of pyramid = √[(height)2 + (side/2)2] = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 cm

⇒ Area of a triangular face = 1/2 × side × slant height = 1/2 × 10 × 13 = 65 cm2

∵ A square pyramid have four triangular faces & a square base,

Total surface area of pyramid = 4(65) + 100 = 360 cm2

∴ the correct answer is 360 cm2.

questions.question: The total weight of 30 students of a class is 360 kg. When the weight of their class teacher is added, the average weight of the group is seen to be 14 kg. What is the class teacher's weight in kg?
questions.questionHtml: The total weight of 30 students of a class is 360 kg. When the weight of their class teacher is added, the average weight of the group is seen to be 14 kg. What is the class teacher's weight in kg?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Old average of 30 students = 360 ÷ 30 = 12 kg.

New average of 31 persons = 14 kg (an increase of 2 kg).

Teacher's weight = New Average + (Number of students × Increase in average)

⇒ Teacher's weight = 14 + (30 × 2) = 14 + 60 = 74 kg.

∴ The correct answer is 74 kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total weight of 30 students = 360 kg

Average weight of 31 persons (30 students + 1 teacher) = 14 kg

Formula Used:

Total Weight = Average × Number of persons

Calculations:

⇒ Total weight of 31 persons = 31 × 14 = 434 kg

⇒ Weight of the class teacher = Total weight of 31 persons − Total weight of 30 students

⇒ Weight of the class teacher = 434 − 360 = 74 kg

∴ The correct answer is 74 kg.

Additional Information

Average Formula

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Net Change Method for Addition

Value of new entity = New Average + Old Number of Entities × Change in Average.

Replacement Method

Value of New Entity = Value of Old Entity + Total Number of Entities × Change in Average.

questions.question: Male and female population of a city is increased by 50% and 20% respectively in 2017 from 2016 and male population in 2016 was 40% more than female population, then by what percent total population of the city is increased in 2017?
questions.questionHtml: Male and female population of a city is increased by 50% and 20% respectively in 2017 from 2016 and male population in 2016 was 40% more than female population, then by what percent total population of the city is increased in 2017?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Male to Female population in 2016 = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5.

We can use the weighted average method to find the net percentage change directly:

Overall % increase = [(Ratio of Male × % change in Male) + (Ratio of Female × % change in Female)] ÷ Total Ratio

Overall % increase = [(7 × 50) + (5 × 20)] ÷ (7 + 5)

Overall % increase = (350 + 100) ÷ 12 = 450 ÷ 12 = 37.5%.

∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Male population in 2016 is 40% more than female population.

Male population increased by 50% and female population increased by 20% in 2017.

Formula Used:

Percentage Increase = (Net Increase ÷ Initial Value) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the female population in 2016 be 100x.

⇒ Male population in 2016 = 100x + (40% of 100x) = 140x.

⇒ Total population in 2016 = 100x + 140x = 240x.

⇒ In 2017, male population = 140x + (50% of 140x) = 140x + 70x = 210x.

⇒ In 2017, female population = 100x + (20% of 100x) = 100x + 20x = 120x.

⇒ Total population in 2017 = 210x + 120x = 330x.

⇒ Net increase in total population = 330x − 240x = 90x.

⇒ Percentage increase = (90x ÷ 240x) × 100 = (9 ÷ 24) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%.

∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.

Additional Information

Percentage Change

The formula for finding the net percentage change of any value is calculated as: [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Weighted Average in Percentage

If a total quantity is split into multiple parts in the ratio w1 : w2, and their individual percentage changes are p1% and p2%, the net percentage change of the entire group is (w1p1 + w2p2) ÷ (w1 + w2).

Base Shift Concept

When calculating percentage increases for two different components, always remember that their percentage values act upon their respective initial base numbers, not on the combined group total.

questions.question: 6 persons running around a ground complete one round in 6, 10, 12, 18, 30 and 40 minutes respectively. After how much time will they meet for the first time if they started running at the same time?
questions.questionHtml: 6 persons running around a ground complete one round in 6, 10, 12, 18, 30 and 40 minutes respectively. After how much time will they meet for the first time if they started running at the same time?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The time taken by the runners to meet for the first time at the starting point is simply the LCM of their individual round times.

Required time = LCM(6, 10, 12, 18, 30, 40)

Required time = 360 minutes

Time in hours = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 hours

∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Times taken by 6 persons to complete one round = 6, 10, 12, 18, 30, and 40 minutes.

Formula Used:

Time to meet again at the starting point = LCM of individual times to complete one round.

Calculations:

⇒ We need to find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 6, 10, 12, 18, 30, and 40.

⇒ Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 10 = 2 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 22 × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 32

⇒ Prime factorization of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 40 = 23 × 5

⇒ LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved.

⇒ Highest power of 2 = 23

⇒ Highest power of 3 = 32

⇒ Highest power of 5 = 5

⇒ LCM = 23 × 32 × 5 = 8 × 9 × 5 = 360 minutes.

⇒ Converting the time into hours = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.

Additional Information

Meeting at the Starting Point on Circular Track

When multiple people are moving around a circular track starting at the same time and place, they meet at the starting point simultaneously after a time equal to the LCM of the times taken by each to complete one round independently.

First Meeting Anywhere on Circular Track

If two runners move in the same direction, the time to meet for the first time anywhere on the track = Track Length ÷ (S1 − S2). If they move in opposite directions, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S1 + S2).

LCM Formula for Fractions

If the individual completion times are given as fractions, you can find the meeting time using: LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

questions.question: The length of a minute hand of a wall clock is 9 cm. What is the area swept (in cm 2 ) by the minute hand in 20 minutes ? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.questionHtml: The length of a minute hand of a wall clock is 9 cm. What is the area swept (in cm<sup>2</sup>) by the minute hand in 20 minutes ? (Take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The minute hand covers a full 360° circle in 60 minutes.

Fraction of circle swept in 20 minutes = 20 ÷ 60 = 1/3 of the total area.

Area swept = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r2

Area = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × (9)2

Area = 3.14 × 27 = 84.78 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 84.78 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of minute hand (radius), r = 9 cm

Time = 20 minutes

Value of π = 3.14

Formula Used:

Angle swept by minute hand in 1 minute = 360° ÷ 60 = 6°

Area of a sector = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr2

Calculations:

⇒ Angle swept in 20 minutes (θ) = 20 × 6° = 120°

⇒ Area swept = (120° ÷ 360°) × 3.14 × (9)2

⇒ Area swept = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × 81

⇒ Area swept = 27 × 3.14

⇒ Area swept = 84.78 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 84.78 cm2.

Additional Information

Clock Angles

The minute hand of a clock moves 6° per minute, while the hour hand moves 0.5° per minute. This relative speed concept is key to solving all clock-based angle problems.

Area of Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ is directly proportional to the angle and is calculated using the formula (θ ÷ 360°) × πr2.

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc corresponding to a central angle θ represents the distance moved along the circumference and is given by (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from Bangalore and Chennai and proceed towards each other at the speeds of 80 km/h and 95 km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is:
questions.questionHtml: Two trains start at the same time from Bangalore and Chennai and proceed towards each other at the speeds of 80 km/h and 95 km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed.

Difference in Speed = 95 − 80 = 15 km/h.

Total Speed = 95 + 80 = 175 km/h.

Total Distance = (Total Speed ÷ Difference in Speed) × Difference in Distance

Total Distance = (175 ÷ 15) × 180 = 175 × 12 = 2100 km.

∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of first train = 80 km/h

Speed of second train = 95 km/h

Difference in distance travelled at meeting time = 180 km

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Let the time taken for both trains to meet be t hours.

⇒ Distance covered by first train = 80 × t

⇒ Distance covered by second train = 95 × t

⇒ The difference in distance covered = 95t − 80t = 15t

⇒ 15t = 180

⇒ t = 180 ÷ 15 = 12 hours

⇒ Total distance between Bangalore and Chennai = 80t + 95t = 175t

⇒ Total distance = 175 × 12

⇒ Total distance = 2100 km

∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S1 − S2|).

Constant Time Property

If two objects travel for the exact same amount of time, the ratio of distances they cover is equal to the ratio of their respective speeds (D1 ÷ D2 = S1 ÷ S2).

questions.question: In an equilateral triangle XYZ, if the length of the circumradius is 10 units and the length of the inradius is 5 units, What is the length of side XY?
questions.questionHtml: In an equilateral triangle XYZ, if the length of the circumradius is 10 units and the length of the inradius is 5 units, What is the length of side XY?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In an equilateral triangle, the circumradius (R) is directly related to the side length (a) by the property R = a / √3.

Given the circumradius R = 10 units, we substitute this value directly into the relation.

⇒ 10 = a / √3

⇒ a = 10√3 units

∴ The correct answer is 10√3 units.

Alternate Method

Given:

Circumradius (R) = 10 units

Inradius (r) = 5 units

Formula Used:

For an equilateral triangle of side length a:

Circumradius (R) = a / √3

Inradius (r) = a / (2√3)

Calculations:

Using the circumradius formula to find the side length:

⇒ R = a / √3

⇒ 10 = a / √3

⇒ a = 10√3 units

We can also verify this using the given inradius:

⇒ r = a / (2√3)

⇒ 5 = a / (2√3)

⇒ a = 5 × 2√3 = 10√3 units

Both parameters perfectly confirm that the length of the side XY (a) is 10√3 units.

∴ The correct answer is 10√3 units.

Additional Information

Area of Equilateral Triangle

The area is calculated using the side length (a) with the formula: Area = (√3 / 4) × a2.

Altitude of Equilateral Triangle

The perpendicular height or median of the triangle is given by the expression: h = (√3 / 2) × a.

Relation between Circumradius and Inradius

In any equilateral triangle, the circumradius (R) is exactly double the length of the inradius (r), establishing the ratio R = 2 × r.

Points of Concurrency

For an equilateral triangle, the centroid, circumcenter, incenter, and orthocenter all coincide perfectly at the same central point.

questions.question: Rs. 1092 is divided among 2 men, 6 women and 8 boys so that the share of a man, a woman and a boy are in the ratio 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 1 . Then, how much does a man get? (In Rs.)
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 1092 is divided among 2 men, 6 women and 8 boys so that the share of a man, a woman and a boy are in the ratio 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 1. Then, how much does a man get? (In Rs.)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total equivalent ratio units = (2 × 3) + (6 × 2) + (8 × 1) = 6 + 12 + 8 = 26 units.

Value of 26 units = ₹1092.

Value of 1 unit = 1092 ÷ 26 = ₹42.

Share of 1 man = 3 units = 3 × 42 = ₹126.

∴ The correct answer is ₹126.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total amount to be divided = ₹1092

Number of people = 2 men, 6 women, and 8 boys

Ratio of individual shares (1 Man : 1 Woman : 1 Boy) = 3 : 2 : 1

Calculations:

Let the share of 1 man, 1 woman, and 1 boy be 3x, 2x, and 1x respectively.

⇒ Total share of 2 men = 2 × 3x = 6x

⇒ Total share of 6 women = 6 × 2x = 12x

⇒ Total share of 8 boys = 8 × 1x = 8x

⇒ Total amount distributed = 6x + 12x + 8x = 26x

⇒ 26x = 1092

⇒ x = 1092 ÷ 26 = 42

⇒ Share of a man = 3x = 3 × 42 = 126

∴ The correct answer is ₹126.

Additional Information

Amount Distribution

When dividing a total amount among different groups of people, always multiply the individual share ratio by the number of people in each group to find the overall ratio in which the total sum is split.

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, it is known as a compound ratio. For a : b and c : d, the compound ratio is (a × c) : (b × d).

Proportion

Four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion if a : b = c : d, which means the product of the extremes equals the product of the means (a × d = b × c).

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 4,000 becomes Rs. 4,960 in 4 years at simple interest. If the rate of interest becomes 1.5 times of itself, then how much this sum will become after 4 years?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 4,000 becomes Rs. 4,960 in 4 years at simple interest. If the rate of interest becomes 1.5 times of itself, then how much this sum will become after 4 years?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Original Simple Interest = 4960 − 4000 = Rs. 960

Since Simple Interest is directly proportional to the rate, New Interest = 1.5 × 960 = Rs. 1440

New Amount = Principal + New Interest = 4000 + 1440 = Rs. 5440

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5,440.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = Rs. 4000

Original Amount (A) = Rs. 4960

Time (T) = 4 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = Principal + SI

Calculations:

⇒ Original SI = Amount − Principal = 4960 − 4000 = Rs. 960

⇒ 960 = (4000 × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 960 = 160 × R

⇒ R = 960 ÷ 160 = 6%

⇒ New Rate = 1.5 × 6% = 9%

⇒ New SI = (4000 × 9 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ New SI = 40 × 36 = Rs. 1440

⇒ New Amount = P + New SI = 4000 + 1440 = Rs. 5440

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5,440.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of Interest, and T is Time. The total amount A is calculated as A = P + SI.

Direct Proportionality in SI

Since SI is directly proportional to Rate (R), if Principal and Time remain constant, increasing the rate by a factor of n will increase the simple interest by the exact same factor n.

Compound Interest vs Simple Interest

Simple interest remains constant for each successive year, whereas compound interest increases every year because it is calculated on the updated amount (Principal + previous Interest).

questions.question: A vessel can be filled by a tap A in 8 minutes, and by another tap B in 10 minutes. A third tap C can empty the vessel in 4 minutes. If all taps are opened simultaneously when the vessel is half full, then which of the following is true?
questions.questionHtml: A vessel can be filled by a tap A in 8 minutes, and by another tap B in 10 minutes. A third tap C can empty the vessel in 4 minutes. If all taps are opened simultaneously when the vessel is half full, then which of the following is true?

options.text: The vessel will be filled in 20 minutes.

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Capacity = LCM(8, 10, 4) = 40 units.

Efficiency of taps → A: +5, B: +4, C: −10.

Net efficiency = 5 + 4 − 10 = −1 unit/min (Negative means vessel empties).

Since the vessel is half full, volume to empty = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 units.

Time to empty the vessel = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is emptied in 20 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by tap B to fill the vessel = 10 min

Time taken by tap C to empty the vessel = 4 min

The vessel is half full initially.


Tap Time (min) Total Capacity Efficiency
A 8 40 +5
B 10 +4
C (Empty) 4 −10

Calculations:

⇒ Net efficiency of all taps together = 5 + 4 − 10 = −1 unit/min.

⇒ A negative efficiency indicates that the vessel is being emptied.

⇒ Quantity of water in the half-full vessel = 40 × (1/2) = 20 units.

⇒ Time required to empty the vessel = Total water ÷ Effective efficiency

⇒ Time = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is emptied in 20 minutes.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its part filled in 1 hour is 1/x. If it empties a full tank in y hours, its part emptied in 1 hour is −1/y.

Net Work Method

Net part filled in 1 hour by both pipes = (1/x) − (1/y). If the result is positive, the tank is being filled. If negative, it is being emptied.

Total Capacity (LCM Method)

Total capacity is assumed to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of all given individual times. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time taken.

questions.question: Two individuals, A and B, have rented a field. A places 12 horses for 5 months and 20 sheep for 4 months. B places 15 cows for 6 months and 30 sheep for 3 months. If 3 horses consume the same food as 5 cows and 6 cows consume the same food as 10 sheep, find what portion of the rent A should pay ?
questions.questionHtml: Two individuals, A and B, have rented a field. A places 12 horses for 5 months and 20 sheep for 4 months. B places 15 cows for 6 months and 30 sheep for 3 months. If 3 horses consume the same food as 5 cows and 6 cows consume the same food as 10 sheep, find what portion of the rent A should pay ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert all animals to Cows (C) to find the total equivalent consumption ratio.

Given 3H = 5C ⇒ 1H = 5/3 C, and 10S = 6C ⇒ 1S = 3/5 C.

A's usage = [12 × (5/3) × 5] + [20 × (3/5) × 4] = 100 + 48 = 148 cow-months.

B's usage = (15 × 6) + [30 × (3/5) × 3] = 90 + 54 = 144 cow-months.

Ratio of rent A : B = 148 : 144 = 37 : 36.

∴ The correct answer is 37/73.

Alternate Method

Given:

A places 12 horses for 5 months and 20 sheep for 4 months.

B places 15 cows for 6 months and 30 sheep for 3 months.

3 horses consume same as 5 cows, and 6 cows consume same as 10 sheep.

Formula Used:

Rent Share Ratio = (Number of animals × Time × Consumption rate)

Calculations:

⇒ Let us convert the number of all animals into equivalent number of Cows (C) for simplicity.

⇒ 3 Horses = 5 Cows ⇒ 1 Horse = 5/3 Cows

⇒ 10 Sheep = 6 Cows ⇒ 1 Sheep = 3/5 Cows

⇒ Equivalent animals placed by A in terms of cows:

⇒ 12 Horses = 12 × (5/3) = 20 Cows

⇒ 20 Sheep = 20 × (3/5) = 12 Cows

⇒ Total equivalent consumption by A = (20 Cows × 5 months) + (12 Cows × 4 months)

⇒ A's total units = 100 + 48 = 148 cow-months

⇒ Equivalent animals placed by B in terms of cows:

⇒ 15 Cows = 15 Cows

⇒ 30 Sheep = 30 × (3/5) = 18 Cows

⇒ Total equivalent consumption by B = (15 Cows × 6 months) + (18 Cows × 3 months)

⇒ B's total units = 90 + 54 = 144 cow-months

⇒ Ratio of rent (A : B) = 148 : 144

⇒ Simplifying by dividing both terms by 4, Ratio = 37 : 36

⇒ Portion of rent A should pay = A's share ÷ (A's share + B's share)

⇒ A's portion = 37 ÷ (37 + 36) = 37/73

∴ The correct answer is 37/73.

Additional Information

Partnership Rent Rule

When multiple people rent a common property (like a pasture), the rent paid by each person is directly proportional to the number of resources used multiplied by the duration of usage (Rent ≈ Animals × Time).

Compound Ratio Equivalency

If distinct categories are given (like Horses, Cows, and Sheep), establish a single common base unit by utilizing equivalent ratios. Converting all distinct variables into one unified variable simplifies compound calculations.

questions.question: Mohan can complete the work in 28 days, and Rohan can complete the work in 56 days, if Sohan is 60% more efficient than Rohan then in how many days Mohan and Sohan can complete the 90% of the work?
questions.questionHtml: Mohan can complete the work in 28 days, and Rohan can complete the work in 56 days, if Sohan is 60% more efficient than Rohan then in how many days Mohan and Sohan can complete the 90% of the work?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Total Work = LCM(28, 56) = 56 units.

Efficiency of Mohan = 56 ÷ 28 = 2 units/day, and Rohan = 56 ÷ 56 = 1 unit/day.

Sohan is 60% more efficient than Rohan, so Sohan's efficiency = 1 × 1.6 = 1.6 units/day.

Combined efficiency of Mohan and Sohan = 2 + 1.6 = 3.6 units/day.

Time = (90% of Total Work) ÷ (Combined Efficiency) = 50.4 ÷ 3.6 = 14 days.

∴ The correct answer is 14 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Mohan to complete the work = 28 days

Time taken by Rohan to complete the work = 56 days

Sohan is 60% more efficient than Rohan.

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

Let Total Work be the LCM of the time taken by Mohan and Rohan.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Mohan 28 56 2
Rohan 56 1

⇒ Efficiency of Rohan = 1 unit/day

⇒ Sohan's efficiency = Rohan's efficiency + 60% of Rohan's efficiency

⇒ Sohan's efficiency = 1 + 0.6 = 1.6 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of Mohan and Sohan = 2 + 1.6 = 3.6 units/day

⇒ Work to be completed = 90% of Total Work = (90 ÷ 100) × 56 = 50.4 units

⇒ Time taken by Mohan and Sohan = Work to be completed ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 50.4 ÷ 3.6 = 14 days

∴ The correct answer is 14 days.

Additional Information

Work and Efficiency Ratio

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a person is x% more efficient, their time taken will be proportionally less. Ratio of efficiency = 100 : (100 + x).

Combined Work Rule

When multiple people work together, their one-day work (efficiency) is simply added up. The total time taken to complete a specific task is derived by Total Target Work ÷ Sum of their individual efficiencies.

questions.question: What should come in place of both x in the equation \(\rm \frac{x}{\sqrt{128}}=\frac{\sqrt{162}}x{}\) ?
questions.questionHtml: What should come in place of both x in the equation \(\rm \frac{x}{\sqrt{128}}=\frac{\sqrt{162}}x{}\)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cross-multiply the given values to solve for x2 directly:

x2 = √128 × √162 = √(128 × 162)

x2 = √(64 × 2 × 81 × 2) = √(64 × 81 × 4)

x2 = 8 × 9 × 2 = 144

x = √144 = 12

∴ The correct answer is 12.

Alternate Method

Given:

x / √128 = √162 / x

Calculation:

⇒ Cross-multiplying both sides, we get:

⇒ x × x = √128 × √162

⇒ x2 = √(128 × 162)

⇒ Factorizing the numbers into perfect squares:

⇒ x2 = √(64 × 2 × 81 × 2)

⇒ x2 = √(64 × 81 × 4)

⇒ Taking the square root of the perfect squares:

⇒ x2 = 8 × 9 × 2

⇒ x2 = 144

⇒ x = √144

⇒ x = 12

∴ The correct answer is 12.

Additional Information

Multiplication of Surds

When multiplying square roots, you can combine them under a single root: √a × √b = √(a × b). This helps in factoring out perfect squares easily.

Perfect Squares Identification

Breaking down large numbers into products of known perfect squares (like 64 = 82 and 81 = 92) simplifies square root calculations significantly without needing prime factorization.

Solving Quadratic Variables

An equation of the form x2 = a2 generally has two roots: x = a and x = −a. In quantitative aptitude simplification questions, the positive root is usually considered unless options suggest otherwise.

questions.question: At a dinner party, every two guests used a bowl of rice between them, every three guests used a bowl of dal among them and every four guests used a bowl of curd among them. There are altogether 65 bowls. What is the number of guests present at the party?
questions.questionHtml: At a dinner party, every two guests used a bowl of rice between them, every three guests used a bowl of dal among them and every four guests used a bowl of curd among them. There are altogether 65 bowls. What is the number of guests present at the party?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the total number of guests be the LCM of 2, 3, and 4, which is 12 units.

Number of bowls used = (12 ÷ 2) + (12 ÷ 3) + (12 ÷ 4) = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13 units.

Given total bowls = 65, so we equate: 13 units = 65 ⇒ 1 unit = 5.

Total guests = 12 units = 12 × 5 = 60 guests.

∴ The correct answer is 60 guests.

Alternate Method

Given:

One bowl of rice is shared between 2 guests.

One bowl of dal is shared among 3 guests.

One bowl of curd is shared among 4 guests.

Total number of bowls used = 65.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total number of guests present at the party be x.

⇒ Number of rice bowls = x/2

⇒ Number of dal bowls = x/3

⇒ Number of curd bowls = x/4

⇒ Total bowls = x/2 + x/3 + x/4 = 65

⇒ Taking the LCM of the denominators 2, 3, and 4, which is 12:

⇒ (6x + 4x + 3x) ÷ 12 = 65

⇒ 13x ÷ 12 = 65

⇒ 13x = 65 × 12

⇒ x = (65 × 12) ÷ 13

⇒ x = 5 × 12

⇒ x = 60

∴ The correct answer is 60 guests.

Additional Information

LCM Method for Equations

Multiplying fractional terms by the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their denominators converts them into whole numbers, making linear equations easier to solve.

Unitary Method

A technique that involves finding the value of a single unit first, and then multiplying it by the total parts to find the desired quantity. If n units = Total, then 1 unit = Total ÷ n.

Fractions in Sharing Problems

When items are shared among a group, the total items used equals the group size divided by the number of people sharing each individual item (Total Items = Total People ÷ Group Size per Item).

questions.question: A, B and C can reap a field in 2 days; B, C and D in 3 days; C, D and A in 7 days; D, A and B in 10 days. In what time can A, B, C and D together reap it?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can reap a field in 2  days; B, C and D in 3 days; C, D and A in 7 days; D, A and B in 10 days. In what time can A, B, C and D together reap it?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Total Work = LCM(2, 3, 7, 10) = 210 units.

Sum of 1-day work (efficiencies) of all 4 groups = (210 ÷ 2) + (210 ÷ 3) + (210 ÷ 7) + (210 ÷ 10) = 105 + 70 + 30 + 21 = 226.

Since each person is included in exactly 3 groups, their combined actual efficiency = 226 / 3 units/day.

Time required = Total Work ÷ Actual Efficiency = 210 ÷ (226 / 3) = 630 / 226 days.

∴ The correct answer is 630/226 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by (A + B + C) = 2 days

Time taken by (B + C + D) = 3 days

Time taken by (C + D + A) = 7 days

Time taken by (D + A + B) = 10 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A + B + C 2 210 105
B + C + D 3 70
C + D + A 7 30
D + A + B 10 21

⇒ Sum of the efficiencies = 105 + 70 + 30 + 21 = 226 units/day

⇒ (A + B + C) + (B + C + D) + (C + D + A) + (D + A + B) = 226

⇒ 3A + 3B + 3C + 3D = 226

⇒ 3 × (A + B + C + D) = 226

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B + C + D) = 226 / 3 units/day

⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 210 ÷ (226 / 3)

⇒ Time required = (210 × 3) / 226 = 630 / 226 days

∴ The correct answer is 630/226 days.

Additional Information

Time and Work LCM Method

Always assume Total Work as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the given days to make calculations fraction-free. Efficiency is calculated as Total Work ÷ Time.

Combined Group Work Principle

When individuals work in overlapping pairs or triplets, sum their combined group efficiencies and divide by the frequency of each person's appearance to find the actual joint efficiency.

Work and Time Relationship

Time and efficiency are inversely proportional. A higher combined efficiency directly results in proportionally less time taken to complete the assigned task.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CDAB'. 

Key Points

  • Sentence C comes first as it introduces the topic of the paragraph, i.e., Maps. 
  • Sentence D follows C as it begins with the word 'or' and D is just another way of saying the previous statement. 
  • Sentence A follows D as it begins with the conjunction 'but' and states that the reduction mentioned in D is done very carefully. 
  • Sentence B follows A as it tells that the reduction is only possible when a small distance on paper represents a large distance on the ground. 
  • Thus, the sequence becomes:
    • C: Maps are drawings, which reduce the entire world or a part of it to fit on a sheet of paper.​
    • D: Or we can say maps are drawn to reduced scales.
    • A: But this reduction is done very carefully so that the distance between the places is real.
    • B: It can only be possible when a small distance on paper represents a large distance on the ground.


Important Points

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
  • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the paragraph and eliminate the irrelevant options.
  • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences of the paragraph (concluding sentence).
  • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants. Identify the pronouns connecting the sentences with one other.

questions.question: What will come in blank (1)?
questions.questionHtml: What will come in blank (1)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Quagmire'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage describes a situation involving a "scramble to assert maritime claims" over trade routes and mineral wealth. This suggests a complex, difficult, and potentially trapped environment.
  • "Quagmire" (नाज़ुक स्थिति/दलदल) refers to a soft boggy area of land that yields underfoot, or metaphorically, an awkward, complex, or hazardous situation from which it is difficult to extricate oneself. This perfectly fits the "geopolitical scramble" mentioned.
  • "Sinecure" (आराम की नौकरी) is a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit. This is logically irrelevant to a global resource scramble.
  • "Cynosure" (आकर्षण का केंद्र) refers to a person or thing that is the center of attention or admiration. While the Arctic is a center of attention, "quagmire" better captures the difficulty and conflict implied by the word "scramble."
  • "Paradigm" (प्रतिमान) is a typical example or pattern of something. While the Arctic is a new pattern of conflict, it is a neutral term that doesn't reflect the "high-stakes scramble" as accurately as "quagmire."
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.
Complete Passage: The precipitous melting of the polar ice caps has fundamentally transformed the Arctic from a peripheral, frozen wasteland into a central geopolitical (1) Quagmire. As the "Great Thaw" accelerates, global powers are no longer merely observers of climate change but active participants in a high-stakes scramble to assert maritime claims over newly accessible trans-continental trade routes and vast, untapped mineral wealth. This environmental metamorphosis represents a profound strategic restructuring of international relations, where the once-impenetrable ice is replaced by overlapping zones of national interest. Given the extreme sensitivity of this frontier, it is essential that the Arctic Council (2) __________ a binding framework that prioritizes ecological preservation over short-term resource extraction.

However, the cooperative spirit of the past is under duress; not only (3) __________ the territorial disputes intensifying among the littoral states, but the increasing militarization of the Northern Sea Route also threatens the long-standing "Arctic Exceptionalism" that once kept the region insulated from global friction. The deployment of ice-class warships and the reopening of Cold War-era outposts signal a shift from scientific collaboration to securitized competition. Any attempt by a single nation to exploit the region’s sub-seabed resources without a robust, multilateral consensus will likely prove to be a (4) __________, leading to a cascade of irreversible environmental damage and a diplomatic fallout that would resonate far beyond the high latitudes.

 
Additional Information
  • Precipitous (तेजी से): Done suddenly and without careful consideration; in this context, it refers to the very fast melting of ice.
  • Maritime Claims (समुद्री दावे): Assertions of sovereignty or control over specific areas of the ocean and the resources beneath them.
  • Metamorphosis (कायापलट): A change of the form or nature of a thing or person into a completely different one.

  • Option 1 ("should formulate") is a common auxiliary usage in British English, but in competitive exams like CAT/GMAT, the pure subjunctive "formulate" is considered more accurate and formal.
  • Option 3 ("is formulating") and Option 4 ("to formulate") are grammatically incorrect within the specific requirements of a subjunctive "that" clause.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

As the "Great Thaw" accelerates, global powers are no longer merely observers of climate change but active participants in a high-stakes scramble to assert maritime claims over newly accessible trans-continental trade routes and vast, untapped mineral wealth. This environmental metamorphosis represents a profound strategic restructuring of international relations, where the once-impenetrable ice is replaced by overlapping zones of national interest.   • Arctic Council: A high-level intergovernmental forum that addresses issues faced by the Arctic governments and the indigenous people of the Arctic.

Key Points

  • Inversion Rule: The auxiliary verb is placed before the subject. In this case, the subject is "the territorial disputes," which is a plural noun.
  • Since the subject is plural, the plural auxiliary verb "are" is required before the subject to maintain subject-verb agreement.
  • Option 2 ("is actually") is singular and fails the agreement test with "disputes".

  • Littoral States (तटीय राज्य): Countries that have a coastline on a particular sea or ocean. For the Arctic, these include Russia, Canada, the US, Norway, and Denmark (via Greenland).
  • Arctic Exceptionalism: The geopolitical concept that the Arctic should be treated as a zone of high cooperation and low tension, separate from the conflicts occurring in the rest of the world.

There’s more than the 101 - seater dining table at the Falaknuma palace that is awe ______. The library done in rosewood and mahogany is a place that will force anyone to ______, if only to admire the fine original polish, the furniture and the walnut carved high roof. questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'inspiring; pause; imitation'.

Key Points 

The completed sentence would be:

There’s more than the 101-seater dining table at the Falaknuma palace that is awe inspiring. The library done in rosewood and mahogany is a place that will force anyone to pause, if only to admire the fine original polish, the furniture, and the walnut carved high roof. The last is supposedly an imitation of the one at Windsor Castle.

Option 1) provides the most suitable words to convey the intended meaning, describing the dining table and library as inspiring and prompting a pause to admire them. Additionally, it suggests that the library is an imitation of the one at Windsor Castle.

inspiring - Evoking or generating feelings of inspiration, motivation, or awe; serving as a source of inspiration. In the context of the sentence, it suggests that there are elements in the Falaknuma palace that are awe-inspiring or capable of inspiring admiration or wonder.

pause - A temporary break or cessation in activity; a momentary stop or hesitation. In the sentence, it suggests that the library in the palace is so impressive that it would make anyone pause or momentarily stop to appreciate its beauty.

imitation - The act of replicating or mimicking something, often with the intention of resembling or copying the original. Here, it refers to the fact that the high roof in the palace is designed to resemble or imitate the one found in Windsor Castle.

Therefore, the correct option 1) "inspiring; pause; imitation" accurately conveys the intended meaning of the sentence. It describes elements in the palace that inspire awe, invites one to pause and admire, and highlights the imitation of the high roof as a design element.
